question: A newly formed community health committee has stopped arguing and is now setting clear operational rules. Which stage of development are they in?

options.A: Storming
options.B: Norming
options.C: Forming
options.D: Adjourning

explanation: During the norming stage, the team establishes rules, resolves past conflicts, and builds a cooperative working relationship. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why should a researcher talk openly about the limitations of their study?

options.A: Delete the entire section if unexpected errors occurred
options.B: Pretend the study was completely flawless to impress readers
options.C: Acknowledge study flaws openly to show scientific integrity
options.D: Blame the research participants for making mistakes

explanation: No study is 100% perfect! Being honest about your weak spots actually builds trust and shows you really know your stuff.

question: A patient has a pressure sore with a thick layer of black dead tissue covering the base. What action is needed first for effective healing?

options.A: Applying dry gauze directly over the black tissue
options.B: Debridement to remove the dead tissue
options.C: Immediate closure with skin grafts without cleaning
options.D: Soaking the entire wound in hydrogen peroxide daily

explanation: That black dead tissue (eschar) acts like a shield trapping bacteria and blocking new growth. It has to be safely cleared away (debrided) before healing can truly begin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h5)

question: Which mask must nurses wear during procedures that generate aerosols on COVID-19 patients?

options.A: Plastic face shield alone
options.B: Cloth face covering
options.C: Standard paper surgical mask
options.D: N95 respirator

explanation: Procedures that kick tiny droplets into the air require a tight-fitting N95 mask to keep you safe. Safety first in nursing! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h7)

question: How does long-term intestinal schistosomiasis end up causing portal hypertension?

options.A: Adult worms multiply rapidly inside the heart and increase overall blood pressure.
options.B: Intestinal bleeding drains blood volume, forcing the heart to pump at a dangerous rate.
options.C: The kidneys fail to filter salt, causing fluid overload throughout the entire body.
options.D: Trapped eggs cause liver fibrosis that blocks blood flow through the portal vein system.

explanation: When eggs get trapped in the liver, the body forms scar tissue (fibrosis). This traffic jam blocks normal blood flow, raising pressure in the portal vein. Pathophysiology made clear!

question: Why are maternity homes so important in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They replace federal tertiary teaching hospitals completely
options.B: They eliminate the need for any medications during labor
options.C: They offer free surgical care funded by international donors
options.D: They serve as local bridges to care when distant hospitals are hard to reach

explanation: Spot on! By being close by, they bridge the gap so mums don't have to travel huge distances just to get basic care.

question: Why is precise documentation of lung assessment findings critical in nursing practice?

options.A: It ensures safe continuity of care and provides a legal record
options.B: It eliminates the need to report changes to the medical doctor
options.C: It proves the nurse spent a long time at the bedside
options.D: It guarantees that diagnostic tests will no longer be necessary

explanation: Clear documentation gives healthcare team members accurate baseline data to track changes in client condition over time safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which hormone acts like a natural relaxant to keep the uterus calm during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone is the uterus's best friend—it keeps everything calm and relaxed until it's time to meet the baby. Keep up the fantastic work!

question: What is the first step a nurse should take when counseling a client on family planning?

options.A: Choose a contraceptive method for the client without asking questions
options.B: Lecture the client on the economic dangers of large families
options.C: Refer the client immediately to a surgeon for sterilization
options.D: Assess the client's medical history and reproductive goals

explanation: Safe and effective counseling must begin with understanding the individual client's health background and personal preferences. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h6)

question: Why should nurses avoid using heavy medical jargon when explaining family planning options to a client?

options.A: To ensure the client fully understands and can make an informed choice
options.B: To prove that nurses have advanced university education
options.C: To save time during busy morning clinic consultations
options.D: To prevent the client from asking questions about side effects

explanation: Spot on! Speaking in plain, simple language empowers our clients to take charge of their own bodies and health decisions.

question: Which part of the teenage brain develops early and drives strong emotions and the search for excitement?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The occipital lobe
options.C: The prefrontal cortex
options.D: The limbic system

explanation: You got this! The limbic system matures early in adolescence, making emotions intense and driving reward-seeking before the brain's rational control center is fully grown.

question: Why is it better for nurses to advocate together through an organization rather than fighting alone at the bedside?

options.A: It removes the legal duty of care from individual practitioners
options.B: It prevents hospital management from ever questioning a nurse
options.C: It guarantees that all patient complaints are immediately dismissed
options.D: It gives nurses a stronger political voice to influence health laws

explanation: Politicians and policy-makers listen much more closely to an organized group representing thousands of healthcare workers than to a single voice!

question: What is the main physical state behind chronic insomnia?

options.A: Hyperarousal
options.B: Parasympathetic dominance
options.C: Hypoglycemia
options.D: Metabolic slowdown

explanation: Chronic insomnia keeps the body in a state of 'hyperarousal'—meaning your nervous system stays stuck on high alert, even when you're trying to rest in bed.

question: Why can prolonged isolation during a hospital stay negatively impact physical recovery?

options.A: Loneliness and lack of social support can worsen stress and delay healing
options.B: Patients without visitors automatically stop taking prescribed drugs
options.C: Social isolation directly causes elevated blood glucose levels
options.D: Isolation increases the body's need for intravenous fluids

explanation: Psychosocial distress triggers physiological stress responses that can weaken immunity and slow down recovery times. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care when a patient has stable tachycardia?

options.A: Restrict all oral fluid intake to lower the circulating blood volume
options.B: Encourage strenuous physical exercise to strengthen the heart muscle
options.C: Identify and treat the underlying trigger while monitoring vital signs
options.D: Immediately apply external defibrillator pads to shock the heart

explanation: A fast heart rate is usually a warning sign of something else—like pain, fever, or stress. Finding and treating that root cause is always our priority!

question: What is the purpose of flashing lights (photic stimulation) during an EEG?

options.A: To warm up the conductive paste on the scalp
options.B: To trigger abnormal brain waves using flashing lights
options.C: To measure how fast the pupils dilate in bright light
options.D: To help the client relax into a deep sleep state

explanation: Sometimes brains need a little nudge to show what they do under stress. Flashing lights at different speeds can help bring out hidden seizure patterns.

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning right after an abortion?

options.A: Patients lose natural immunity without hormonal birth control
options.B: Hormonal pills speed up physical recovery from a miscarriage
options.C: Fertility returns very quickly after an abortion procedure
options.D: Patients are required by law to start birth control immediately

explanation: Ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion! That means a patient can get pregnant again before their next period even arrives.

question: Which type of incontinence happens when a person leaks urine while coughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy objects?

options.A: Stress urinary incontinence
options.B: Functional urinary incontinence
options.C: Urge urinary incontinence
options.D: Overflow urinary incontinence

explanation: Stress incontinence is triggered by physical movements that suddenly push down on the bladder when pelvic support is weak. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: Which federal law requires healthcare facilities to inform patients about advance directives upon admission?

options.A: The Patient Self-Determination Act
options.B: The Nursing Practice Act
options.C: The Health Insurance Portability Act
options.D: The Affordable Care Act

explanation: Passed in 1991, the Patient Self-Determination Act ensures that patients are told about their right to make advance directives when entering a healthcare facility. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended nursing approach when correcting common contraceptive myths?

options.A: Validating the client's underlying concerns
options.B: Insulting the client for believing rumors
options.C: Providing clear and accurate health facts
options.D: Explaining normal physiological side effects

explanation: Insulting clients creates a hostile environment and drives them away from formal healthcare facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h7)

question: Which sign tells you that a child's breathing problem is getting worse and turning into respiratory failure?

options.A: Slow, irregular breathing and cyanosis
options.B: An increase in spontaneous talking
options.C: Loud, powerful crying and high energy
options.D: Rapid, deep breathing with normal skin color

explanation: At first, a struggling child breathes super fast. But once their muscles get too tired, they slow down, breathe irregularly, and turn blue (cyanosis). That's a true emergency!

question: When looking at needle sizes, what does a higher gauge number tell you?

options.A: The bevel angle is sharper
options.B: The needle length is longer
options.C: The needle width is smaller
options.D: The barrel capacity is larger

explanation: Needle gauges can trick people, but just remember: the bigger the gauge number, the tinier and thinner the actual needle! A 27-gauge is super fine, while an 18-gauge is quite thick.

question: Which gene mutations are most strongly linked to a higher risk of ovarian cancer?

options.A: BRCA1 and BRCA2
options.B: HER2 and KRAS
options.C: TP53 and EGFR
options.D: APC and MLH1

explanation: Spot on. Inherited mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes significantly increase a woman's lifetime chance of developing both breast and ovarian cancers.

question: Why are concentrated electrolytes considered 'high-alert' medications even though they aren't narcotics?

options.A: Patients often try to steal them for recreational use at home
options.B: They spoil very quickly when exposed to normal room air and light
options.C: Simple dosing mistakes with these drugs can cause severe patient harm or death
options.D: They are extremely expensive for the hospital to purchase and restock

explanation: Even a tiny calculation error with concentrated electrolytes can be fatal. That's why we treat them with extra caution!

question: What is the main difference between sampling error and sampling bias?

options.A: Sampling error only happens in qualitative studies, while bias happens in quantitative studies
options.B: Sampling error is caused by dishonest participants, while bias is caused by computer glitches
options.C: Sampling bias can be completely avoided with large samples, while error cannot be fixed
options.D: Sampling error is natural random variation, while sampling bias is a systematic flaw in selection

explanation: Spot on! Error is just normal luck of the draw, but bias means your method had a unfair lean that messed up the results.

question: What do we call an endocrine disorder that starts directly inside the target gland itself?

options.A: Tertiary disorder
options.B: Idiopathic disorder
options.C: Primary disorder
options.D: Secondary disorder

explanation: When a gland like the adrenal cortex acts up on its own instead of waiting for brain signals, doctors call it a primary disorder. Simple and clear!

question: What is the most important nursing duty right after a patient has a bone marrow test?

options.A: Stop them from drinking any fluids for 12 hours
options.B: Take off the pressure dressing in five minutes
options.C: Get them up to do heavy exercises
options.D: Watch the puncture site closely for bleeding

explanation: Because the needle goes right into the bone, keeping an eye on the site for bleeding or swelling is a top priority to keep your patient safe.

question: Why do nurses advise wearing cotton underwear when dealing with a yeast infection?

options.A: Cotton underwear prevents systemic absorption of the prescribed oral tablets
options.B: Cotton allows air circulation and keeps the area dry, which discourages yeast growth
options.C: Cotton fibers directly release natural antifungal chemicals onto the skin
options.D: Synthetic fabrics chemically bind to antifungal creams and block their action

explanation: Yeast loves warm, dark, and moist places. Breathable cotton keeps things cool and dry, making it a hostile home for yeast!

question: Who is widely recognized as the pioneer of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Mary Seacole
options.B: Linda Richards
options.C: Clara Barton
options.D: Florence Nightingale

explanation: Florence Nightingale transformed nursing during the Crimean War by emphasizing sanitation, organization, and formal training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: What creates the direct pathway for spreading disease during an unsafe injection?

options.A: Inhaling medication droplets while prepping a syringe
options.B: A contaminated needle breaking the skin and entering circulation
options.C: Swallowing oral tablets without enough water
options.D: Touching a sealed medication package with bare hands

explanation: Spot on! Injections bypass your skin's natural defense barrier, meaning any germs on a dirty needle go straight into the patient's tissues and bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of a bag-valve-mask (BVM) resuscitator?

options.A: To measure blood oxygen saturation
options.B: To deliver positive pressure ventilation
options.C: To visualize the vocal cords clearly
options.D: To suction thick oral secretions

explanation: Great job! You squeeze the BVM manually to push air into the lungs of a patient who cannot breathe on their own. Simple and lifesaving! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h2)

question: Why are pencil-point spinal needles often preferred over cutting needles?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of infection
options.B: They are cheaper to manufacture
options.C: They inject medication twice as fast
options.D: They separate dura fibers rather than cutting them

explanation: Pencil-point needles part the dural fibers, lowering the amount of cerebrospinal fluid leakage and reducing headache risks. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h4)

question: How do calcium channel blockers work to treat angina?

options.A: By speeding up the movement of sodium ions
options.B: By blocking adrenaline receptors in the brain
options.C: By adding extra calcium back into the bloodstream
options.D: By preventing calcium from causing muscle contraction

explanation: Calcium is what muscles need to squeeze tight. By blocking it, these drugs help blood vessels and heart muscle relax.

question: Why do young teens sometimes look a bit clumsy or awkward?

options.A: The brain shrinks temporarily during a growth spurt
options.B: Bones grow faster than the supporting muscles and tendons
options.C: Vision blurs due to rapid eyeball enlargement
options.D: Inner ear fluid production increases rapidly

explanation: Correct! Their bones shoot up faster than their muscles can keep up with, which temporarily throws off their balance and coordination.

question: What does a general survey primarily evaluate?

options.A: The patient's complete financial and employment history
options.B: The microscopic cellular structure of body tissues
options.C: The patient's overall appearance and obvious behavior
options.D: The exact electrical conduction system of the heart

explanation: The general survey is a quick visual overview of how sick, comfortable, or distressed a patient looks right away. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: What special X-ray technology does the radiologist use to watch the barium move in real-time?

options.A: Thermography
options.B: Electrocardiography
options.C: Fluoroscopy
options.D: Magnetic resonance

explanation: Keep it up! Fluoroscopy is basically an X-ray movie, letting the doctor watch the drink flow through your system live. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the medical name for the bluish color you see on a patient's skin when they lack oxygen?

options.A: Jaundice
options.B: Pallor
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Erythema

explanation: Cyanosis comes from 'cyano' (blue). It happens when red blood cells lacking oxygen circulate near the skin surface. A classic clinical sign to remember!

question: What term describes the physical need for higher doses of a drug to get the same effect?

options.A: Tolerance
options.B: Intoxication
options.C: Withdrawal
options.D: Dependence

explanation: Tolerance happens when the body gets used to a drug, requiring larger amounts to produce the original feeling. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h1)

question: A patient gets amoxicillin plus clavulanic acid for a tough infection. What does clavulanic acid do?

options.A: It acts as a mild sedative to help the patient rest
options.B: It increases urine production to flush out bacterial toxins
options.C: It blocks bacterial enzymes that normally destroy amoxicillin
options.D: It numbs local pain at the site of the infected tissue

explanation: Clavulanic acid is a trusty shield! It stops stubborn bacteria from producing enzymes that would normally chew up and destroy amoxicillin.

question: Which of these is a WRONG practice when it comes to preventing poisoning?

options.A: Using clear labeling on all containers holding hazardous substances
options.B: Storing kerosene and bleach in empty soft drink bottles in the kitchen
options.C: Consulting qualified health workers before taking herbal concoctions
options.D: Keeping all pharmaceutical drugs locked up away from children

explanation: You got it! Putting dangerous chemicals in drink bottles is a recipe for disaster. Always keep them in their original, clearly labeled containers.

question: What is a key difference between benign and malignant tumors?

options.A: Malignant tumors stay completely contained within a capsule
options.B: Malignant tumors never grow back after simple removal
options.C: Benign tumors do not spread to distant parts of the body
options.D: Benign tumors always require immediate chemotherapy

explanation: A great way to remember this in the wards is that benign tumors stay put and grow slowly. Malignant tumors are the ones that can invade other tissues and spread around.

question: How can severe kidney problems in an expectant mother directly hurt her baby?

options.A: By passing high levels of urea directly into the fetal stomach
options.B: By reducing blood supply and nutrient delivery across the placenta
options.C: By triggering early closure of the fetal cardiac chambers
options.D: By increasing the amount of amniotic fluid to dangerous levels

explanation: When the mother's kidneys and blood pressure struggle, the placenta doesn't get enough blood flow, which means the baby gets less of what it needs to grow strong.

question: What is a referral in the context of family planning?

options.A: Directing a client to another facility when needs exceed current capacity
options.B: Ordering a new brand of oral contraceptive pills from the pharmacy
options.C: Discharging a client completely from the healthcare system
options.D: Scheduling a routine return visit for the same clinic next month

explanation: A referral happens when a client needs specialized care or resources that the current primary facility cannot provide. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: A patient with a peripheral IV line says it hurts, and you notice the area is cool, pale, and swollen. What has likely happened?

options.A: Air embolism
options.B: Circulatory overload
options.C: Phlebitis
options.D: Infiltration

explanation: You got it! When the IV fluid slips out of the vein and leaks into the surrounding tissue, it makes the skin feel cool, tight, and swollen.

question: What two main elements make up the foundation of modern professional nursing?

options.A: Art and science
options.B: Administration and finance
options.C: Theory and politics
options.D: History and geography

explanation: Nursing combines the emotional and human connection of art with the empirical clinical knowledge of science to care for patients effectively. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h1)

question: How does myocarditis usually affect the function of the heart muscle?

options.A: It thickens the coronary arteries completely
options.B: It turns the heart muscle hard like bone
options.C: It weakens the muscle walls and lowers pumping efficiency
options.D: It permanently opens up all the valves

explanation: Because inflammation damages the muscle tissue, the heart struggles to squeeze hard, leading to reduced pumping power. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which of these actions breaks patient confidentiality in home care?

options.A: Closing the bedroom door before conducting a physical exam
options.B: Discussing a patient's medical condition with a neighbor outside
options.C: Asking family members to step out during a private assessment
options.D: Locking clinical notes inside the nursing bag

explanation: Correct! Gossiping or sharing private health details with neighbors is a serious breach of trust and confidentiality.

question: Which nursing intervention provides a simple, non-pharmacological method to relieve primary dysmenorrhea?

options.A: Administering intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Placing the client in an absolute flat supine position
options.C: Encouraging immediate high-impact interval training
options.D: Applying local heat therapy to the lower abdomen

explanation: Heat relaxes uterine smooth muscle and helps reduce the ischemic pain associated with menstrual cramps. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h7)

question: How does community health nursing mainly differ from taking care of patients at the bedside?

options.A: It focuses on the health needs of a whole population
options.B: It focuses on the personal career goals of the nurse
options.C: It diagnoses just one single patient at a time
options.D: It manages the financial budget of the hospital

explanation: You've got this! While bedside nursing cares for one person at a time, community nursing looks at the big picture to help entire neighborhoods and groups stay healthy.

question: What is the correct way to feel (palpate) lymph nodes during a physical exam?

options.A: Scratching firmly across the skin surface with fingernails
options.B: Pinching the skin tightly between thumb and index finger
options.C: Using the finger pads in gentle circular motions
options.D: Pressing hard with a single thumb until the patient winces

explanation: Always use gentle circular motions with your finger pads. This helps you roll the nodes against the tissue underneath without pushing them away or hurting the patient.

question: A nurse organizes a stress-management workshop for workers facing imminent factory closures. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Primary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Curative prevention

explanation: Spot on! Primary prevention focuses on stopping health problems before they start by promoting healthy coping strategies early on. Excellent! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h5)

question: How long should children wash their hands with soap to properly get rid of germs?

options.A: Twenty seconds
options.B: Ten seconds
options.C: One hour
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Twenty seconds is the magic number! Singing a short song helps kids scrub long enough to break down the germs on their skin.

question: What are the three classic signs of bacterial meningitis?

options.A: Tremors at rest, slow movement, and rigid limbs
options.B: Chronic cough, chest pain, and night sweats
options.C: Sudden weight gain, hair loss, and dry skin
options.D: Severe headache, high fever, and stiff neck

explanation: Keep this classic triad in mind: headache, fever, and a stiff neck (nuchal rigidity). Whenever you see these together in a test or ward, think meningitis!

question: Which attitude is most important for a nurse during post-abortion counseling?

options.A: Non-judgmental and empathetic
options.B: Skeptical and questioning
options.C: Indifferent and detached
options.D: Strictly authoritative and firm

explanation: Being warm, kind, and non-judgmental builds trust, making the patient feel safe to share their worries and ask questions.

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classic 5 Ps assessed during neurovascular checks?

options.A: Pallor
options.B: Pulselessness
options.C: Perspiration
options.D: Pain

explanation: The 5 Ps stand for Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, and Paralysis. Perspiration is not part of this assessment. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h6)

question: A young female patient has Chlamydia. What is the standard medical treatment?

options.A: A series of therapeutic vaccines given over a six-month recovery period
options.B: Strict bed rest and immune-boosting vitamins with no prescription medications
options.C: A course of oral antibiotics for the patient and treatment for her recent sexual partners
options.D: Surgical drainage of infected cervical cysts followed by topical anti-fungals

explanation: Chlamydia is caused by bacteria, so it needs antibiotics! Always remember to treat sexual partners too, otherwise, they'll just pass it right back.

question: When caring for a survivor of sexual assault, what should be the primary focus of the nurse during the physical assessment?

options.A: Focusing entirely on gathering legal evidence without offering comfort
options.B: Finishing the examination as fast as possible regardless of patient consent
options.C: Preventing re-traumatization while providing compassionate, trauma-informed care
options.D: Convincing the patient to forget the event and return home immediately

explanation: Trauma-informed care prioritizes the patient's emotional safety, consent, and control to avoid causing further psychological harm during the exam. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T9#GNS312_U4_T9_h4)

question: Why do nurses track CD4 T-cell counts regularly during antiretroviral therapy?

options.A: To evaluate the recovery and strength of the immune system
options.B: To predict how much weight the patient will gain
options.C: To decide if the patient needs immediate blood transfusions
options.D: To calculate the exact date the patient was infected

explanation: You've got this! Tracking CD4 counts is like checking the health score of the immune system to see how well it's bouncing back.

question: What is the normal expected time for capillary refill when you press on a healthy nail bed?

options.A: Less than two seconds
options.B: Exactly five seconds
options.C: Between six and ten seconds
options.D: Up to fifteen seconds

explanation: Quick color return (under two seconds) means blood is flowing nicely to the fingertips!

question: What usually happens in a ward that is poorly organized?

options.A: Doctors take over all daily medication administration tasks
options.B: Patient recovery times become much shorter automatically
options.C: Staff experience chaos and higher risks of clinical errors
options.D: Nurses have more time to spend on personal rest breaks

explanation: Spot on! When things lack structure, confusion creeps in, tasks get missed, and mistakes happen. Good organization keeps everyone safe.

question: How do peer educators help drive the elimination of harmful practices at the village level?

options.A: By communicating health messages in relatable, culturally familiar ways
options.B: By performing surgical reversals of genital mutilation in homes
options.C: By issuing official fines to families who violate public health laws
options.D: By writing academic textbooks for university nursing students

explanation: Peers are trusted members of the community who can discuss sensitive topics without sounding judgmental or foreign. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h5)

question: Why is giving plain water unnecessary for a fully breastfed infant living in a very hot climate?

options.A: Infants cannot swallow water safely during their first few months
options.B: Breast milk is made mostly of water and satisfies the infant's thirst
options.C: Hot weather stops the infant from feeling thirsty
options.D: Water causes immediate stomach pain in newborn babies

explanation: Breast milk contains about eighty-eight percent water, which is more than enough to keep a baby hydrated even in hot weather. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: Which inhalation device requires the patient to take a fast, forceful breath to activate medication delivery?

options.A: Dry Powder Inhaler
options.B: Metered-dose inhaler with spacer
options.C: Simple nasal cannula
options.D: Standard nebulizer machine

explanation: Dry Powder Inhalers rely entirely on the patient's own inhalation effort to pull the powder out of the device and into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the term for a dangerous loop where low blood pressure weakens the heart, which then lowers blood pressure even further?

options.A: An adaptive resting phase
options.B: A normal healthy recovery process
options.C: A stable metabolic equilibrium
options.D: A positive feedback spiral toward shock

explanation: You've got it! This is a classic runaway positive feedback loop where each problem makes the next one worse, pulling the patient deeper into danger if we don't intervene.

question: How do vision changes in macular degeneration (AMD) differ from cataracts?

options.A: AMD affects side vision first, while cataracts ruin night vision.
options.B: AMD causes sudden total blindness overnight, while cataracts take years.
options.C: AMD affects central vision, while cataracts cause overall blurriness and glare.
options.D: AMD causes intense eye pain, whereas cataracts are painless.

explanation: Macular degeneration targets your sharp central focus (like when reading), leaving side vision alone. Cataracts, on the other hand, just make everything look foggy and hazy.

question: What is the immediate sign that you have accidentally hit the sciatic nerve during a gluteal injection?

options.A: Sharp, burning pain shooting down the patient's leg
options.B: Instant swelling and bright red blood spurting out
options.C: A loud popping sound coming from the hip joint
options.D: The syringe plunger becoming completely jammed

explanation: Spot on. Hitting the sciatic nerve causes an electric, burning shock down the leg. If this happens, stop and withdraw immediately!

question: When is the best time to bring in palliative care for a patient diagnosed with lymphoma?

options.A: Only during the final 24 hours of life
options.B: Alongside regular curative treatment right from the start
options.C: Only when the patient asks for hospice
options.D: After all chemotherapy options have failed

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for end-of-life; it's about comfort and symptom relief, and it works best when started early alongside cancer treatment!

question: Why do patients often feel sudden cramping when the scope enters the sigmoid colon?

options.A: The scope has to poke through the muscular wall.
options.B: The natural S-curves and movement of this bowel make it sensitive to stretching.
options.C: The rectum is completely bypassed.
options.D: Numbing medicine causes muscle spasms.

explanation: Exactly! Navigating those twists and turns stretches the bowel wall a bit, which triggers nerves and causes temporary cramping. Totally normal response!

question: What are individual and psychological causes of conflict mostly rooted in?

options.A: The official hospital building blueprint and layout
options.B: Government policies regarding nurse salaries
options.C: The exact number of beds available in the ward
options.D: Personal values, perceptions, and individual goals

explanation: These triggers come from within each person—how we view situations, what we value most, and what we personally want to achieve.

question: What happens if a nurse chooses a stockinette that is too narrow for a patient's leg?

options.A: It will dissolve when the plaster gets wet
options.B: It can squeeze the limb and restrict blood circulation
options.C: It will automatically stretch to fit any size perfectly
options.D: It will fall off the leg before the cast is applied

explanation: An undersized stockinette acts like a tourniquet when stretched tightly over a limb, cutting off proper blood flow. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical result of a major homeostatic breakdown?

options.A: Uncontrolled blood sugar spikes
options.B: Dangerous shifts in blood pH
options.C: Severe dehydration
options.D: Balanced electrolyte levels in the blood

explanation: You got it! Balanced electrolytes mean homeostasis is winning and doing its job, not that it has broken down.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal use for sedative medications?

options.A: Treating bacterial infections
options.B: Stopping active epileptic seizures
options.C: Managing acute and chronic anxiety
options.D: Inducing sleep during short-term insomnia

explanation: Sedatives only calm the nervous system. They do not kill bacteria—that is a job for antibiotics! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is a very important self-care habit to teach a patient who cannot feel their feet?

options.A: Washing with harsh antiseptic spirit daily
options.B: Checking the feet every single day for cuts and sores
options.C: Walking barefoot to make the soles tougher
options.D: Soaking feet in hot water to boost blood flow

explanation: Since they won't feel pain from a thorn or scrape, daily mirror checks help catch injuries before they turn into bad ulcers. You are learning real patient care!

question: Which of these is an early warning sign that conflict is brewing on a ward?

options.A: Nurses eagerly volunteering to help each other with heavy tasks
options.B: Staff members starting a shared book club
options.C: An increase in overall patient satisfaction scores
options.D: Passive-aggressive notes and increased sarcasm during handovers

explanation: Sarcasm, eye-rolling, and sticky notes left behind are classic signs that team members are starting to rub each other the wrong way.

question: Why should we make sure marginalized or vulnerable groups have a voice in community health committees?

options.A: They usually have the largest financial donations to give
options.B: International donors refuse to fund homogeneous committees
options.C: They often experience the highest burden of disease and need a voice
options.D: It is the only way to meet nursing licensure requirements

explanation: Exactly. Vulnerable groups often face the toughest health challenges, so their unique needs must be heard to make our nursing care truly effective.

question: Why should every task on a project checklist be assigned to a specific person?

options.A: To make it easier to fire workers who make minor mistakes
options.B: To ensure only the facility director does any actual work
options.C: To ensure accountability so responsibilities are never neglected
options.D: To prevent team members from communicating with each other

explanation: When everyone is responsible, no one is responsible! Assigning names ensures every important task actually gets done.

question: Which of these is NOT a core duty expected of a nurse, no matter where they work?

options.A: Performing major neurosurgical operations independently
options.B: Administering prescribed medications safely
options.C: Advocating for the health and safety of patients
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and clinical progress

explanation: Surgeries like brain operations are strictly done by trained surgeons, not nurses, regardless of whether it's a primary clinic or a tertiary hospital!

question: Why do doctors and nurses prefer feeding patients through the gut (enteral nutrition) rather than through a drip (parenteral nutrition) when possible?

options.A: It requires no special monitoring of blood glucose or laboratory tests
options.B: It helps maintain gut health and prevents bacteria from escaping into the body
options.C: It completely eliminates the risk of aspiration or gastrointestinal upset
options.D: It is absorbed directly into the bloodstream without needing digestion

explanation: Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut lining strong and stops bad bacteria from wandering where they shouldn't!

question: Which action by a nurse best demonstrates ongoing support for a grieving family after their loved one has passed away?

options.A: Encouraging them to forget the loss and return to work quickly
options.B: Billing the family promptly for grief counseling services
options.C: Sending a sympathy card or making a follow-up phone call weeks later
options.D: Avoiding contact to give them complete isolation

explanation: Small acts of ongoing outreach, such as a card or call, show the family they are remembered and supported through their grief journey. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h8)

question: What is the biggest danger when an atherosclerotic plaque suddenly bursts open in a heart artery?

options.A: The heart rate slows down dramatically from nerve signals
options.B: The artery immediately widens and causes blood pressure to drop
options.C: A blood clot forms quickly over the break and blocks blood flow
options.D: Red blood cells leak directly into the chest cavity

explanation: When a plaque ruptures, the body treats it like an injury and forms a clot right there. Unfortunately, that clot can block the artery and cause a heart attack.

question: What is a crucial safety check before using any mechanical lift sling?

options.A: Ensuring the patient is wearing non-skid slippers
options.B: Inspecting the straps and clips for fraying or damage
options.C: Measuring the exact distance to the hallway door
options.D: Checking if the battery is fully charged to maximum speed

explanation: Always double-check those straps! Frayed or worn fabric can snap under pressure, which is dangerous for the patient in the sling.

question: What is the correct compression-to-breath ratio for single-rescuer adult CPR?

options.A: 5 compressions to 1 breath
options.B: 100 compressions to 5 breaths
options.C: 30 compressions to 2 breaths
options.D: 15 compressions to 2 breaths

explanation: The golden rule for adult BLS is 30 chest compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. You'll memorize this in no time!

question: Which of the following actions is NOT appropriate when a nurse discovers a severely irregular pulse in a resting patient?

options.A: Notify the attending physician promptly about the irregular rhythm
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.C: Review the medication record for heart-altering drugs
options.D: Assess the patient for dizziness, chest pain, or shortness of breath

explanation: Waiting to report an acute abnormal finding puts the patient at risk; abnormal signs require prompt assessment and notification. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h6)

question: As a nurse preparing a mother for discharge, what is one of your most important responsibilities?

options.A: Ensuring the mother can name critical danger signs for herself and the baby
options.B: Confirming that lochia has completely stopped entirely
options.C: Scheduling permanent sterilization procedures before she leaves
options.D: Providing enough formula for the first three months of life

explanation: Before anyone goes home, we must make sure they know the warning signs to watch for so they can run back to the hospital if something goes wrong. Excellent safety practice! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: Why is studying maternal morbidity just as crucial as looking at maternal mortality?

options.A: Morbidity data is much easier to collect in rural hospitals than mortality numbers
options.B: Mortality rates have dropped to zero globally, making morbidity the only priority
options.C: It focuses solely on the health status of the newborn baby after delivery
options.D: It highlights the hidden burden of long-term suffering and disability survivors face

explanation: For every woman who sadly passes away, many more live with severe, lifelong health issues from pregnancy complications. Understanding this helps us provide better care for mothers in our communities!

question: What is the medical term for the slowness of voluntary movement seen in Parkinson's patients?

options.A: Akathisia
options.B: Dyskinesia
options.C: Ataxia
options.D: Bradykinesia

explanation: Great word to know! 'Brady' means slow, and 'kinesia' means movement. Together, bradykinesia means it takes a patient much longer to start and finish simple physical actions.

question: About how many extra calories a day are needed in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: Three hundred calories
options.B: Two thousand calories
options.C: One thousand calories
options.D: Fifty calories

explanation: Spot on! An extra 300 calories a day—like a small, nourishing snack—is usually all it takes to fuel the final trimesters.

question: If a patient cannot speak, which physical sign might tell you they are in pain?

options.A: Deep, slow, and relaxed breathing
options.B: Low blood pressure and calm posture
options.C: Tachycardia and facial grimacing
options.D: Warm and dry skin on the hands

explanation: Spot on! When patients can't talk, their body speaks for them—look out for a fast heart rate (tachycardia) and tight, frowning facial expressions.

question: Why is cultural awareness so important for nursing students?

options.A: Nurses care for diverse patients from many different backgrounds
options.B: It stops students from ever arguing about medical facts
options.C: Lecturers grade you based on your cultural heritage
options.D: The hospital requires everyone to speak three local languages

explanation: As a nurse, you will meet patients from all walks of life. Understanding their cultures helps you give kind, respectful care to everyone.

question: Why are infrared thermometers a lifesaver when taking a child's temperature?

options.A: Under-fives cannot register a fever on other devices
options.B: Infrared devices block all room drafts completely
options.C: Children are less likely to get scared or fight you
options.D: Kids' skin always radiates extra heat

explanation: Quick, touch-free readings mean less anxiety and crying for the little ones, making your assessment much smoother!

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing consideration related to postpartum endocrine changes?

options.A: Monitoring for sudden increases in maternal blood pressure caused by rising placental hormone levels
options.B: Observing for successful milk let-down reflex stimulated by infant suckling and oxytocin
options.C: Reassuring the mother about normal physiological changes during her hospital recovery
options.D: Assessing for signs of postpartum mood changes linked to rapid estrogen and progesterone withdrawal

explanation: Placental hormone levels drop rapidly after delivery, not rise. Therefore, rising placental hormone levels are not a concern postpartum. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h6)

question: A mother of four girls visits the clinic complaining of constant headaches, tiredness, and sleeplessness, but tests show she is physically fine. What should you, as the nurse, keep in mind?

options.A: Nutritional deficiencies caused exclusively by eating local foods
options.B: Psychological distress related to family pressure for a male child
options.C: An undiagnosed genetic blood disorder causing sleep disturbances
options.D: A rare neurological reaction to routine postpartum vitamins

explanation: Physical complaints with no clear medical cause often mask deep emotional stress from family pressure to have a boy.

question: Why is building a warm, trusting relationship so important during a health history chat?

options.A: It speeds up the hospital discharge process significantly
options.B: It eliminates the need for a physical examination entirely
options.C: It guarantees the patient will take all prescribed medications
options.D: It encourages the patient to share sensitive details honestly

explanation: You got it! When patients trust you and feel safe, they'll open up about the things that really matter for their care.

question: Which of these is a poor practice when assessing a community's health needs?

options.A: Looking at both clinic records and community interview notes together
options.B: Involving local community health workers in reviewing the findings
options.C: Comparing local disease rates with regional or national averages
options.D: Focusing solely on community problems while ignoring existing local strengths

explanation: Never ignore what a community already does well! Focusing only on problems makes people dependent, rather than empowering them to use their own strengths.

question: An antenatal patient complains that her iron pills make her stool dark and cause mild constipation. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Instruct her to stop taking the medication immediately and discard the remaining pills
options.B: Explain that dark stools are harmless and suggest increasing fluid and fiber intake
options.C: Tell her to double the dose so her body adjusts faster to the iron
options.D: Refer her urgently to the surgeon for a bowel obstruction evaluation

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Dark stools are completely normal with iron supplements. Reassuring the patient and encouraging water and local vegetables/fiber helps her stick to her treatment without fear.

question: Why must reusable equipment like stethoscopes be wiped with disinfectant between patients?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To keep the metal parts from rusting in humid weather
options.C: To remove any manufacturer dust from the surface
options.D: To ensure the sound quality remains clear for hearing

explanation: Medical tools can easily carry germs from one patient to another if they are not cleaned properly. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: What is the most immediate, life-threatening danger for a mother with a placental abnormality?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum depression
options.C: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Urinary tract infection

explanation: When the placenta doesn't attach or separate normally, the womb often struggles to clamp down afterward, leading to heavy, dangerous bleeding. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h7)

question: What is the simplest way to describe what a drug does in the body?

options.A: Any synthetic material used strictly for laboratory testing
options.B: A compound that creates entirely new cellular functions in organs
options.C: Any chemical substance that alters biological function in a living body
options.D: A natural substance derived exclusively from plants for nourishment

explanation: Spot on! Drugs work by modifying what your body is already doing—they don't magically invent brand-new functions. You've got this!

question: What is a common cause of blunt cardiac injury during a motor vehicle accident?

options.A: Inbreathing toxic exhaust fumes from the damaged engine
options.B: The seatbelt cutting directly across the neck muscles
options.C: The driver hitting their chest against the steering wheel
options.D: Sudden exposure to cold air through broken windows

explanation: Direct impact against the steering wheel during rapid deceleration transmits massive blunt force straight through the sternum to the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of regular pacemaker interrogation appointments?

options.A: To surgically replace the battery every six months
options.B: To reprogram the heart muscle to beat much faster
options.C: To check battery life and evaluate device functioning
options.D: To wash the surgical scar and apply fresh bandages

explanation: Interrogation allows healthcare providers to assess remaining battery power, lead performance, and device data. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h8)

question: What does a spiritual assessment in palliative care mostly focus on?

options.A: Memorization of sacred religious texts
options.B: Meaning, purpose, and inner peace
options.C: Regular attendance at local religious services
options.D: Donations made to charitable organizations

explanation: Spirituality isn't just about religion—it's about helping a patient find hope, peace, and meaning in their journey.

question: How has the primary role of the nurse changed from early historical times to today?

options.A: It evolved from informal domestic charity to an autonomous regulated profession
options.B: It changed from independent medical diagnosis to unpaid domestic work
options.C: It shifted from hospital administration to strictly religious duties
options.D: It transformed from a male-only military role to a purely clerical office job

explanation: Think about how far we've come! Modern nursing requires formal education, licensing, and independent critical thinking, rather than just basic home caregiving. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is proper body support so important for patients who spend all day in bed?

options.A: It prevents skin breakdown and joint contractures
options.B: It completely cures chronic bone infections
options.C: It increases the patient's daily calorie intake
options.D: It eliminates the need for daily vital signs

explanation: Great job! Proper support spreads out the patient's weight evenly, keeping pressure sores away and stopping joints from freezing up in stiff positions.

question: Which specific white blood cells does HIV target and attack inside the body?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: CD4+ T lymphocytes
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Platelets

explanation: Spot on! HIV locks onto CD4+ T lymphocytes. As it infects and damages these cells over time, the body's immune system gradually weakens. You've got this!

question: A patient feels a burning, shooting pain down their leg after a back injury. What kind of pain is this?

options.A: Visceral nociceptive pain
options.B: Neuropathic pain
options.C: Referred inflammatory pain
options.D: Acute somatic pain

explanation: Burning, tingling, or shooting pains are classic signs of neuropathic pain, which happens when nerves themselves are irritated or damaged.

question: Which cranial nerve carries hearing and balance signals from the inner ear to the brain?

options.A: Cranial nerve VIII
options.B: Cranial nerve V
options.C: Cranial nerve VII
options.D: Cranial nerve X

explanation: Cranial nerve VIII is the vestibulocochlear nerve. 'Vestibulo' handles balance, and 'cochlear' handles hearing!

question: Why is a complete cure not the main goal of rehabilitation in degenerative genetic conditions?

options.A: Rehabilitation therapies only work on non-genetic illnesses
options.B: Hospitals lack the proper equipment to reverse genetic changes
options.C: Patients refuse to participate in long-term treatment programs
options.D: The conditions involve continuous, progressive breakdown of tissues

explanation: Since these conditions involve ongoing tissue breakdown, therapy is all about managing symptoms and helping patients adapt, rather than fixing the root genetic cause. Keep it up!

question: When a nurse asks a patient, 'What makes your stomach pain better or worse?', what are they checking?

options.A: Severity and duration
options.B: Quality and onset
options.C: Provoking and palliating factors
options.D: Region and radiation

explanation: Spot on! Asking what triggers or relieves the discomfort helps you figure out the provoking (starting) and palliating (soothing) factors.

question: A patient requesting a medical abortion is found to have an IUD in place. What needs to happen first?

options.A: The patient must be switched immediately to a surgical procedure.
options.B: The medications can be given safely around the IUD.
options.C: The IUD must be removed before starting the medications.
options.D: Progesterone supplements should be given to offset the IUD.

explanation: Well done! Any existing intrauterine device (IUD) needs to be removed before starting the regimen to lower the risk of severe infection and make sure the medication works properly.

question: Which common substance must a patient recovering from viral hepatitis strictly avoid?

options.A: Alcohol
options.B: Plain water
options.C: Green vegetables
options.D: Fresh fruits

explanation: You got it! Alcohol is processed directly by the liver, so drinking it adds heavy toxic stress to an organ that is already struggling to heal.

question: Which member of the healthcare team is a medical doctor who specializes in physical medicine and rehab?

options.A: Social worker
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Physiatrist
options.D: Occupational therapist

explanation: A physiatrist is a doctor who leads the medical side of physical medicine and rehabilitation. Great job keeping terms straight!

question: What is a constant physical challenge when nursing on a moving ship?

options.A: Frequent electrical storms inside underground tunnels
options.B: Exposure to extreme desert heat and blowing sand
options.C: Constant rolling, pitching, and vibrating of the vessel
options.D: Lack of oxygen due to high altitude mountain climbing

explanation: Exactly! The natural movement of the water means the ship is always moving, which makes doing clinical procedures a unique challenge.

question: You notice the safety box on your treatment trolley is about three-quarters full. What should you do?

options.A: Seal the container and replace it with a new one
options.B: Push the contents down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.C: Transfer some needles into a regular black plastic bag
options.D: Leave it open until the end of the week to save money

explanation: Safety first! Never push down or overfill sharp containers. Seal them at three-quarters full to prevent accidental needle pricks.

question: What is the leading cause of ongoing back pain and injuries among nursing staff?

options.A: Writing patient reports while sitting on unadjusted chairs
options.B: Walking across slippery hospital floors in soft shoes
options.C: Lifting and moving heavy patients without proper mechanical assistance
options.D: Standing still at the nursing station during long night shifts

explanation: Pulling or lifting heavy patients manually puts massive strain on your lower back. Always use proper leverage, help, or lifting devices!

question: What is the main reason paracetamol (acetaminophen) is different from a true NSAID?

options.A: It causes severe stomach ulcers within hours of use
options.B: It can only be given through intravenous injection
options.C: It completely blocks both COX-1 and COX-2 permanently
options.D: It lacks significant anti-inflammatory properties

explanation: Paracetamol is great for knocking out a fever or a headache, but it doesn't do much for swelling or joint inflammation like ibuprofen does. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge when trying to measure maternal mortality in Nigeria?

options.A: Universal reporting of every home birth through digital apps
options.B: High rates of deliveries occurring outside formal health facilities
options.C: Misclassification of the true cause of death on certificates
options.D: Incomplete or poorly maintained paper registers in hospitals

explanation: We don't yet have universal digital tracking for home births in Nigeria. In fact, the lack of reporting for home births is one of our biggest hurdles!

question: A patient cannot read the written instructions for taking their blood pressure medication. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Scold the patient for not attending school and refusing to learn English
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately without any further medication instructions
options.C: Write the instructions in complex medical terminology for clarity
options.D: Use simple verbal explanations, pictorial charts, and involve a trusted family caregiver

explanation: Wonderful! Using pictures, clear talking points, and family help ensures the patient understands their medication safely.

question: What is the main reason why medication rooms in the ward must always be kept locked?

options.A: To prevent unauthorized access and accidental drug mix-ups
options.B: To make it difficult for doctors to write new prescriptions
options.C: To keep the air conditioning inside the room very cold
options.D: To hide hospital supply costs from incoming student nurses

explanation: Locking the drug room keeps powerful medications safe from unauthorized people and helps keep everything organized for the team.

question: Why can taking NSAIDs frequently lead to stomach ulcers?

options.A: They increase acid production directly in the esophagus
options.B: They stop the liver from producing digestive bile
options.C: They chemically burn the outer walls of the small intestine
options.D: They block prostaglandins that protect the stomach lining

explanation: NSAIDs block helpful body chemicals called prostaglandins. Without them, your stomach lining loses its shield against stomach acid.

question: Which muscle in the bladder wall is the main target for anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Sphincter muscle
options.B: Trigone muscle
options.C: Detrusor muscle
options.D: Ureteral smooth muscle

explanation: Anticholinergics work directly on the detrusor muscle to calm it down and stop involuntary bladder squeezes. You've got this!

question: What is a very common and dangerous late-stage complication for many degenerative brain disorders?

options.A: Rapid nerve regeneration
options.B: Aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Sudden high blood pressure
options.D: Severe weight gain

explanation: When swallowing muscles get too weak, food and saliva can easily slip into the lungs and cause a serious infection called aspiration pneumonia. You are building life-saving knowledge!

question: Why do nurses always warm up peritoneal dialysis fluids before infusing them?

options.A: To kill any bacteria present in the plastic tubing
options.B: To prevent abdominal cramping and patient hypothermia
options.C: To prevent the fluid from turning into a solid gel
options.D: To make the drug dissolve faster inside the IV bag

explanation: Exactly! Putting cold fluid straight into the belly causes painful cramps and can drop the patient's body temperature. Always warm it to body temperature first! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at a primary health clinic presents with facial swelling, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Give her paracetamol tablets and ask her to wait
options.B: Advise her to drink plenty of palm wine and sleep
options.C: Send her home with instructions to rest for a week
options.D: Refer her urgently to a secondary or tertiary facility

explanation: These are signs of severe pre-eclampsia, which can quickly lead to deadly eclamptic seizures if not managed in a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: Why are persistent chronic pain medications often prescribed 'by the clock' rather than 'PRN'?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing extra tablets
options.B: To maintain a steady blood level and prevent pain from returning
options.C: To make medication administration easier for the night shift nurses
options.D: To ensure the patient takes the maximum possible dose every day

explanation: Giving medications on a scheduled, round-the-clock basis prevents peaks and valleys in drug concentration, keeping constant control over chronic pain. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h4)

question: What is a very common trigger for dangerous autonomic dysreflexia in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

options.A: Listening to loud music
options.B: Yawning repeatedly in a quiet room
options.C: A full bladder or constipation
options.D: Eating a cold meal too quickly

explanation: Anything irritating the body below the injury level—like a desperately full bladder or trapped stool—can send the nervous system into a dangerous spike called autonomic dysreflexia.

question: A patient asks why her doctor checked estriol levels specifically during her pregnancy. What is the main source of estriol?

options.A: The anterior pituitary
options.B: The placenta
options.C: The thyroid gland
options.D: The adrenal medulla

explanation: The placenta pumps out loads of estriol during pregnancy. Doctors use it as a helpful check to see how well the baby and placenta are doing!

question: Who is usually the first member of the nursing team to notice small, daily changes in a resident's condition?

options.A: Director of nursing
options.B: Billing administrator
options.C: Facility pharmacist
options.D: Certified nursing assistant

explanation: Certified nursing assistants (CNAs) spend the most time with residents, making them amazing at spotting early signs of a change in health!

question: Among these clinical situations, which one calls for cold therapy instead of heat?

options.A: A fresh ankle sprain from a soccer game
options.B: Generalized joint ache from morning arthritis
options.C: A tense muscle spasm in the upper shoulder
options.D: Chronic lower back stiffness in an older adult

explanation: Great choice! For fresh injuries within the first 48 hours, always reach for the cold pack to control swelling and numb the pain.

question: What is the primary goal of staffing in healthcare management?

options.A: Filling every vacant desk in the hospital
options.B: Matching qualified staff with patient care needs
options.C: Lowering the budget spent on medical equipment
options.D: Reducing the total number of working hours for nurses

explanation: Staffing is fundamentally about putting the right number of skilled workers where they are needed to keep patients safe. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why should a nurse document how well a patient tolerated a physical transfer?

options.A: To prove to the hospital kitchen when meals should be served
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of the nursing care
options.C: To track how the patient handled the activity and monitor for fatigue or pain
options.D: To decide which television channels the patient prefers

explanation: Documenting tolerance helps the whole nursing team know if the patient is gaining strength or getting too exhausted during activities.

question: What is the main purpose of tertiary prevention in nursing care?

options.A: Preventing complications in established chronic diseases
options.B: Curing genetic disorders before birth
options.C: Stopping healthy people from ever getting sick
options.D: Screening asymptomatic populations for hidden risk

explanation: Well done! Tertiary prevention steps in after a diagnosis to help patients manage their condition and avoid further complications.

question: What physical sign should a nurse check for when assessing a patient for fluid overload due to excess salt intake?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Pitting edema in the ankles and shins
options.C: Extreme dryness and cracking of the lips
options.D: Rapid thinning of the fingernail beds

explanation: Fluid retention from excess sodium pooling in the lower extremities commonly presents as pitting edema over bony prominences. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h8)

question: What happens when 'noise' or interference enters the communication process?

options.A: It speeds up how fast the sender talks to the receiver
options.B: It disrupts the message and can lead to misunderstandings
options.C: It changes the communication channel into a written format
options.D: It automatically guarantees the client will follow instructions

explanation: Noise represents any barrier or distraction that gets in the way of clear message transmission between sender and receiver. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: How do conflicts or humanitarian crises usually affect the rate of early marriages in affected areas?

options.A: Rates drop to zero because civil registries completely shut down
options.B: Rates decrease because communities unite to protect children
options.C: Rates tend to rise because families seek protection or financial relief
options.D: Rates remain completely unchanged regardless of external dangers

explanation: Spot on! When families face displacement or insecurity, fear for their daughters' safety and survival often drives them toward early marriage.

question: When you spin a blood sample in a centrifuge, what components make up that thin middle layer called the buffy coat?

options.A: White blood cells and platelets
options.B: Water and dissolved glucose
options.C: Red blood cells and hemoglobin
options.D: Albumin and clotting proteins

explanation: Well done! The buffy coat is that tiny, whitish layer sitting between the clear plasma on top and the heavy red blood cells at the bottom. It holds your infection-fighters (white blood cells) and clotting helpers (platelets).

question: A nursing mum in the clinic needs affordable protein options available in local Nigerian markets. What should you suggest?

options.A: Processed canned biscuits
options.B: Imported energy drink powders
options.C: Packaged artificial sweeteners
options.D: Beans, crayfish, and lean fish

explanation: Local proteins like beans, crayfish, and fish are budget-friendly, easily accessible, and provide wonderful amino acids for lactation.

question: Which medication is often given alongside NSAIDs to stop pericarditis from coming back?

options.A: Warfarin
options.B: Digoxin
options.C: Atropine
options.D: Colchicine

explanation: Colchicine works brilliantly alongside NSAIDs to calm down stubborn inflammation and prevent flare-ups. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why do doctors often order a brain scan before doing a lumbar puncture on a suspected meningitis patient?

options.A: To make sure high pressure in the brain won't cause the brainstem to herniate.
options.B: To warm up the lower back before the needle goes in.
options.C: To measure the exact blood flow through the carotid arteries.
options.D: To completely replace the need to test the cerebrospinal fluid.

explanation: Safety first! If there's too much pressure building up inside the head, draining fluid from the lower back can create a dangerous suction effect, pushing the brain downward. A scan checks if it's safe first.

question: How do sperm mostly travel upward through the uterus toward the fallopian tubes?

options.A: By floating passively in the bloodstream
options.B: By pulling themselves along using specialized cellular feet
options.C: By their own flagellar swimming and aided by uterine muscle contractions
options.D: By relying entirely on gravity within the pelvis

explanation: Exactly! Sperm use their tails to swim, but rhythmic, gentle squeezes of the uterus give them a wonderful transport boost.

question: Which of the following is a common physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Diabetes mellitus
options.B: Drinking adequate water
options.C: Regular aerobic exercise
options.D: Eating fresh fruits daily

explanation: Chronic conditions like diabetes damage blood vessels and nerves over time, making it a major physical risk factor for sexual dysfunction. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h3)

question: Why do doctors choose conservative surgery instead of a full hysterectomy for young patients who want children?

options.A: It removes painful lesions while keeping the uterus and ovaries intact for future pregnancy
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any future hormonal medication
options.C: It guarantees that endometriosis will never return after the procedure
options.D: It is a non-invasive procedure performed without general anesthesia

explanation: Conservative surgery is all about precision: laser away or cut out the bad tissue while protecting the womb and ovaries so she can still get pregnant later.

question: What is the main goal of professional communication in nursing?

options.A: To ensure the doctor has less paperwork to do
options.B: To pass the time during long hospital shifts
options.C: To build trust and coordinate safe patient care
options.D: To prevent patients from asking too many questions

explanation: Spot on! As nurses, everything we say is designed to put the patient at ease and keep their care safe and organized.

question: When is the best time to check the second set of vital signs after starting a blood transfusion?

options.A: After thirty minutes
options.B: At the very end of the bag
options.C: After two hours
options.D: After fifteen minutes

explanation: The 15-minute mark is crucial because most serious acute reactions happen right at the beginning of the infusion.

question: Why do civil lawsuits often name both the nurse and the hospital as defendants?

options.A: Because the hospital shares responsibility for employee actions under institutional liability
options.B: Because hospitals commit more medication errors than individual nurses
options.C: Because nursing councils require hospitals to pay all court fines
options.D: To ensure the nurse does not have to pay any legal fees

explanation: Hospitals usually share the blame (and liability) for mistakes made by their staff during working hours.

question: Which action directly helps keep nurses on the job by letting them have a say in their workplace?

options.A: Involving frontline staff in scheduling committees
options.B: Eliminating all mentorship and peer support programs
options.C: Increasing the number of mandatory night shifts
options.D: Relying entirely on remote electronic surveillance

explanation: When nurses help make decisions that affect their daily lives—like putting together duty rosters—they feel respected and stay longer!

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fever and headache, but is fully alert and able to swallow drugs. How do you classify this?

options.A: Asymptomatic malaria
options.B: Chronic malaria
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Uncomplicated malaria

explanation: Correct! Because the patient is stable and can take oral meds without danger signs, it's uncomplicated malaria. You'll see this a lot in clinical postings!

question: Why do we take a baseline assessment when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: It helps the nurse detect small changes in the patient's condition over time.
options.B: It replaces the need to review previous medical history charts.
options.C: It eliminates the need to perform further physical examinations during the shift.
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will experience a rapid recovery.

explanation: Spot on! A baseline is your starting point. Knowing where your patient starts helps you easily spot if they are getting better or worse during your shift.

question: How does promising strict privacy change how teenagers use reproductive health services?

options.A: It guarantees that teenagers will never experience health complications
options.B: It completely replaces the need for parental guidance at home
options.C: It encourages teens to seek early advice, testing, and care
options.D: It legally forces parents to abandon their teenage children

explanation: When teens know their visit is confidential, they feel safe enough to get timely checkups, contraception, or treatment when they need it. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: Which of these specimens should NOT be put in the refrigerator if transport is delayed?

options.A: Routine urine collection
options.B: Swab of a skin wound
options.C: Stool sample for parasites
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)

explanation: CSF contains very delicate germs that the cold can easily kill. These urgent samples need to stay at room temperature!

question: Which of these conditions is a classic reason to use a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute sinusitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Spot on! Sinusitis brings painful inflammation and blocked nasal passages, which respond wonderfully to the warm, soothing moisture of steam therapy.

question: Why do many women hesitate to go back to a clinic for their next reproductive health checkup?

options.A: Nurses typically encourage too many follow-up visits
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable everywhere
options.C: They prefer managing all medical conditions independently at home
options.D: They experienced poor quality or disrespectful care previously

explanation: It's sad but true—if patients meet rude staff or lack privacy, they lose trust and stay away. Always aim to be the nurse who makes clients feel safe and welcome! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is cost-effectiveness a major factor when choosing essential drugs?

options.A: It guarantees that the manufacturer makes a high profit margin
options.B: It proves that the medicine was manufactured inside the country
options.C: It ensures limited financial resources can treat the maximum number of people
options.D: It eliminates the need for any healthcare workers to monitor patients

explanation: Because healthcare budgets are always restricted, choosing cost-effective options stretches funds to cover more patients in need. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: A clinic notices that the cash counted at day's end is less than the value of drugs sold. What should management do first?

options.A: Stop ordering new medications until patient attendance increases
options.B: Conduct a thorough audit of daily sales records and collection points
options.C: Transfer all pharmacy staff to different departments in the hospital
options.D: Increase the selling price of all essential medicines immediately

explanation: Good clinical management means investigating before accusing! An audit helps you find where money is leaking—whether through errors or missing cash.

question: How often should you reposition a bedbound patient to keep pressure ulcers away?

options.A: Every six hours
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once per shift
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: You got it! Turning your patient at least every two hours takes the heavy pressure off bony areas and gets the blood flowing to their skin again.

question: Why are stool softeners commonly prescribed after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To increase the speed of food digestion in the stomach
options.B: To prevent straining that can disrupt the suture line
options.C: To increase blood flow to the lower limbs
options.D: To cure chronic urinary tract infections

explanation: Avoiding hard stools and straining protects the delicate surgical repairs from tension and tearing. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: Why might a nurse experience ethical conflict when carrying out a patient's request to stop life support?

options.A: Fearing that the hospital will refuse to pay the nurse's salary
options.B: Believing that living wills have no legal standing in a hospital
options.C: Balancing the duty to do no harm with the duty to respect patient choices
options.D: Knowing that doctors are legally required to ignore advance directives

explanation: Nurses want to protect life, so stopping life support can feel emotionally difficult even though respecting the patient's autonomy is legally and ethically correct. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h4)

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the soft spot towards the front of a baby's head)?

options.A: Triangle
options.B: Square
options.C: Circle
options.D: Diamond

explanation: The anterior fontanelle is famously diamond-shaped. This is a classic midwife clue that helps you tell it apart from the triangular posterior fontanelle during an exam!

question: A community health nurse wants to reach residents who never visit the clinic. What is the best first step?

options.A: Conduct house-to-house surveys and community profiling
options.B: Report the entire community to the federal ministry of health
options.C: Wait patiently in the clinic office for someone to ask for help
options.D: Close the primary health center and move to a big city

explanation: Sometimes patients can't or won't come to the clinic. Going out to meet them through home visits and community mapping is the best way to find those who need help the most.

question: How does the lower oesophageal sphincter keep itself tightly closed to stop acid reflux?

options.A: By active mucus production sealing the lower mucosal folds together
options.B: Through intrinsic smooth muscle tone reinforced by the diaphragmatic crura
options.C: By voluntary contraction of skeletal muscle fibers wrapped around the hiatus
options.D: Through continuous parasympathetic stimulation sent by the glossopharyngeal nerve

explanation: You got it! It relies on its own natural muscle tension plus a helpful extra squeeze from the diaphragm opening it passes through.

question: What is the purpose of using the 'teach-back' method during patient education?

options.A: Asking the patient to repeat instructions in their own words
options.B: Testing the patient on medical history terminology
options.C: Reading a medical textbook aloud to the family
