options.D: Having the nurse lecture for an hour without stopping

explanation: Teach-back is brilliant: you ask them to explain your instructions back to you in their own words so you know they truly understand.

question: Which condition is classically associated with a "bird-beak" tapering appearance at the bottom of the esophagus?

options.A: Zenker's diverticulum
options.B: Hiatal hernia
options.C: Gastric ulcer
options.D: Achalasia

explanation: Achalasia prevents the lower esophageal sphincter from opening properly, creating a narrow, bird-beak shape on the X-ray film as barium tries to pass. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h6)

question: What laboratory check is needed to tell Taenia saginata and Taenia solium apart with certainty?

options.A: Performing a chest X-ray to check for lung consolidation
options.B: Checking serum electrolyte levels for chronic dehydration
options.C: Examining the uterine branches of intact passed proglottids
options.D: Measuring total white blood cell counts in a routine blood sample

explanation: You got it! Lab techs count the side branches in the uterus of an intact passed segment to easily tell the two species apart.

question: What is the main role of the nurse in a healthcare team working on medication adherence?

options.A: Isolating the patient from other team members to prevent conflicting advice
options.B: Taking over financial responsibilities to pay for all patient prescriptions
options.C: Acting as the central coordinator who bridges communication between the patient and team
options.D: Prescribing alternative chemical drugs when pharmacy supplies run empty

explanation: Because nurses spend the most time bedside or clinic-side, we are the vital bridge connecting the patient's reality to the rest of the healthcare team.

question: What is a key feature of positive discipline?

options.A: Personal accountability and mutual respect
options.B: Heavy financial fines for minor errors
options.C: Strict reliance on fear and threats
options.D: Immediate suspension without investigation

explanation: Positive discipline encourages workers to take responsibility for their actions through cooperation. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h2)

question: What type of air pressure is kept inside the operating room to stop outside air from rushing in when doors open?

options.A: Positive pressure
options.B: Negative pressure
options.C: Variable pressure
options.D: Neutral pressure

explanation: Positive pressure acts like an invisible shield, pushing air outward when doors open so germs stay out of the sterile theatre. Well done!

question: What is a major reason farm crops get wasted before they ever reach the market?

options.A: Excessive consumer demand in local supermarkets
options.B: Poor storage facilities and inadequate transport networks
options.C: Immediate consumption of all crops by farmers
options.D: Strict government laws against selling fresh crops

explanation: Bad roads and lack of proper storage silos mean harvested food often spoils before getting to people who need it.

question: Why does consciousness usually return very quickly after a person falls flat on the floor?

options.A: Gravity helps blood flow back to the brain in the flat position.
options.B: The sudden impact stimulates the nervous system to wake up.
options.C: Cold air near the floor triggers a reflex response.
options.D: Muscles relax completely and stop consuming extra oxygen.

explanation: Lying flat eliminates the effect of gravity working against blood pressure, quickly restoring circulation to the brain. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why can routine antenatal care alone miss some pregnancy dangers?

options.A: Pregnant women rarely attend clinics during their first trimester
options.B: Antenatal clinics refuse to monitor blood pressure during visits
options.C: Many critical emergencies strike unpredictably without prior warning signs
options.D: Complications only develop after healthcare facilities close for the day

explanation: Even if a pregnancy looks completely healthy, sudden issues like heavy bleeding or high blood pressure can pop up out of nowhere. That is why emergency care is so vital!

question: Which childhood lymphoma is very common in malaria-endemic regions like Nigeria?

options.A: Multiple myeloma
options.B: Chronic myeloid leukemia
options.C: Burkitt lymphoma
options.D: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia

explanation: Burkitt lymphoma is well-known in tropical Africa. It's often linked with the Epstein-Barr virus and chronic exposure to malaria.

question: A patient at 32 weeks reports she has not felt her baby move all day. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Mild physiological anemia of pregnancy
options.B: Potential fetal distress or compromise
options.C: Standard weight gain in the third trimester
options.D: Normal resting behavior of a mature fetus

explanation: Whenever a mom says baby's movements have stopped or slowed right down, treat it as an emergency and check the baby right away.

question: Why is it best to give the HPV vaccine before a person becomes sexually active?

options.A: The vaccine changes its chemical formulation based on sexual history
options.B: Adolescent immune systems cannot process the vaccine after sexual debut
options.C: The vaccine provides the highest protection before any potential exposure to the virus
options.D: Insurance policies refuse coverage for the vaccine once a person turns eighteen

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines work best when your immune system meets the pathogen before the actual virus does.

question: When is a topical drug most likely to cause unexpected whole-body (systemic) side effects?

options.A: When stored at room temperature before application
options.B: When applied in a very thin layer on thick, calloused heels
options.C: When applied over large areas of broken or inflamed skin
options.D: When given to an adult instead of a child

question: What is the primary purpose of data organization in nursing research?

options.A: To publish findings without peer review
options.B: To eliminate the need for statistical testing
options.C: To increase the total number of study participants
options.D: To structure raw information so it can be analyzed

explanation: Organizing raw data transforms messy notes and numbers into a structured format that allows researchers to look for patterns and run accurate analysis. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body make a lot more blood?

options.A: To lower her core body temperature
options.B: To make up for heavy monthly bleeding
options.C: To prevent swollen veins in her legs
options.D: To supply the growing placenta and baby

explanation: A pregnant body increases its blood volume to make sure the placenta and the growing baby get all the oxygen and nutrients they need.

question: How do qualitative and quantitative approaches differ in their main goals?

options.A: Qualitative avoids human subjects while quantitative studies only animals
options.B: Qualitative uses statistical formulas while quantitative uses personal stories
options.C: Qualitative focuses on lab equipment while quantitative focuses on interviews
options.D: Qualitative seeks deep meaning while quantitative seeks prediction and control

explanation: Simply put: qualitative wants to understand the 'why' and 'how' of feelings, while quantitative wants to measure and test facts.

question: What kind of urine do you expect from a patient who is severely dehydrated?

options.A: Small volume and low concentration
options.B: Large volume and low concentration
options.C: Large volume and high concentration
options.D: Small volume and high concentration

explanation: Makes total sense, right? When the body lacks water, the kidneys hold onto every drop, leaving you with a small amount of dark, concentrated urine.

question: What is an important way community health nurses can help prevent FGM?

options.A: Performing mild forms of FGM under hygienic conditions
options.B: Issuing legal certificates permitting traditional circumcisers
options.C: Subsidizing the cost of traditional ceremonies
options.D: Educating local communities about the health risks of FGM

question: What must you always check before involving a partner or family member in a PAC patient's care plan?

options.A: The explicit consent and permission of the client
options.B: Mandatory attendance at a community health seminar
options.C: A written approval letter from the hospital administrator
options.D: Proof of legal marriage verified by hospital registration

explanation: The patient's privacy is paramount. You can never bring family or partners into her care without her clear go-ahead.

question: A patient suddenly falls asleep during the day and feels weak when feeling strong emotions. What condition is this?

options.A: Insomnia
options.B: Narcolepsy
options.C: Somnambulism
options.D: Sleep apnea

explanation: Narcolepsy causes sudden sleep attacks during the day. Strong emotions can sometimes trigger sudden muscle weakness called cataplexy.

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention when caring for patients with sensory loss?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any future medical checkups
options.B: To prevent healthy family members from developing the condition
options.C: To completely reverse the underlying genetic cause of the disease
options.D: To limit disability and maximize remaining functional independence

explanation: Tertiary prevention is all about rehabilitation and helping people live their best, most independent lives even after a permanent loss. You're doing great learning these levels of prevention!

question: What is the first thing you should do when caring for a patient having an Addisonian crisis?

options.A: Administering intravenous hydrocortisone and fluid replacement
options.B: Restricting all oral and intravenous sodium intake immediately
options.C: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to stimulate adrenal output
options.D: Preparing the patient for emergency surgical removal of the pancreas

explanation: Correct! An Addisonian crisis means the body lacks vital cortisol, causing shock and crashing blood pressure. They need IV steroids and fluids right away.

question: A mum receiving oxytocin gets intensely distressed, and the monitor shows late decelerations. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Administer an oral stimulant medication
options.B: Increase the oxytocin drip rate to speed up delivery
options.C: Stop the oxytocin infusion immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to push harder right away

explanation: Stopping the oxytocin stops the strong contractions from straining the uterus further, helping oxygen flow back to the baby.

question: What advice should you give a patient receiving treatment for a bacterial STI regarding sex?

options.A: Resume intercourse immediately once the burning sensation starts to fade
options.B: Limit intercourse to protected methods without needing partner treatment
options.C: Abstain from sexual activity until he and his partner have finished treatment
options.D: Use oil-based lubricants to prevent transmission while taking oral tablets

explanation: No sex until both partners finish their treatment course! This stops the dreaded 'ping-pong' effect of passing the infection right back to each other.

question: What is the main benefit of a multidisciplinary team approach in maternal health?

options.A: It reduces the total number of healthcare facilities needed in a state
options.B: It ensures that only doctors make clinical decisions for patients
options.C: It eliminates the need for any documentation or record keeping
options.D: It combines different professional skills to ensure a safe continuum of care

explanation: Working together allows various cadres to pool their unique skills, supporting the mother effectively across all stages of care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h3)

question: Why is teaching patients about normal aging changes an effective preventive strategy?

options.A: It forces patients to stop all sexual activity as they grow older
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future medical checkups
options.C: It guarantees that older adults will never experience physical illness
options.D: It prevents unnecessary panic and performance anxiety when minor shifts occur

explanation: When patients know what to expect physically as they age, they are less likely to develop psychological anxiety that worsens sexual problems. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h4)

question: What is the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina called?

options.A: The cervix
options.B: The fallopian tube
options.C: The endometrium
options.D: The myometrium

explanation: The cervix forms the lower, narrow portion of the uterus connecting the uterine cavity to the vaginal canal, which is the specific site where cervical cancer originates. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the main medical use for mannitol, a special osmotic diuretic?

options.A: Treating chronic leg swelling from varicose veins
options.B: Lowering high pressure inside the brain
options.C: Lowering blood sugar in diabetic patients
options.D: Managing everyday high blood pressure

explanation: Mannitol acts like a strong magnet, pulling fluid out of swollen brain tissues and into the blood vessels to quickly relieve pressure.

question: What makes potassium-sparing diuretics unique compared to other water pills?

options.A: They prevent the loss of potassium in the urine
options.B: They only work when a patient is fasting
options.C: They completely stop the kidneys from making urine
options.D: They increase blood pressure instead of lowering it

explanation: You've got this! While most diuretics wash away vital potassium along with water, potassium-sparing drugs hold onto that precious potassium.

question: How does the muscle type in the oesophagus change from the top down?

options.A: It remains entirely composed of involuntary smooth muscle.
options.B: It shifts from skeletal muscle to smooth muscle.
options.C: It shifts from smooth muscle to skeletal muscle.
options.D: It remains entirely composed of skeletal muscle fibers.

explanation: You've got this! The top part is skeletal muscle (under our conscious control for swallowing), while the lower two-thirds shift to smooth muscle to automatically push food down.

question: Which IV fluid is the gold standard for fluid resuscitation during the first day of major burn care?

options.A: 5 percent Albumin solution
options.B: Lactated Ringer's solution
options.C: 5 percent Dextrose in Water
options.D: 0.9 percent Normal Saline

explanation: Lactated Ringer's is closest in makeup to our body's own blood plasma, making it the top choice for refilling those empty tanks after a burn.

question: A clinic ensures that all adolescents receive care regardless of their financial status or background. Which core principle does this practice demonstrate?

options.A: Acceptability
options.B: Appropriateness
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Equitability

explanation: Equitability means treating all young clients fairly without discrimination based on status, gender, or ability to pay. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: Which test is mostly used to confirm if a patient has fluid or consolidation in their lungs?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Electrocardiogram
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging

explanation: A simple chest X-ray is fast, easy, and gives a clear picture of cloudy areas or fluid buildup in the lungs.

question: What is the main goal of mobile medical outreaches for persons with disabilities in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: To gather statistical research data without providing direct care
options.B: To replace all permanent primary healthcare clinics in the country
options.C: To conduct advanced surgical operations in local village squares
options.D: To bring essential healthcare services and assistive devices closer to underserved populations

explanation: Outreach brings care right to the doorsteps of people who can't easily travel to big city hospitals. Vital work for community health!

question: What typically happens during the clinical latency stage of an untreated HIV infection?

options.A: The immune system completely clears the virus from the body.
options.B: The patient immediately develops terminal opportunistic infections.
options.C: The virus replicates slowly while the patient may have few symptoms.
options.D: Red blood cells multiply rapidly to compensate for tissue damage.

explanation: Well done! During latency, the virus is still active but multiplies at a low level, and the person might feel completely well for years without treatment.

question: What is the most common medication given sublingually for sudden chest pain?

options.A: Nitroglycerin
options.B: Furosemide
options.C: Metformin
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Nitroglycerin is the classic sublingual drug used to rapidly dilate coronary vessels during angina. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h6)

question: Which of these is a well-known chemical hazard you might find in a clinical area?

options.A: Discarded paper patient admission folders
options.B: Cardboard packaging from intravenous fluids
options.C: Used cotton wool rolls from wound dressing
options.D: Mercury from a broken blood pressure device

explanation: Correct! Heavy metals like mercury—often found in older BP cuffs or thermometers—are toxic chemicals that need careful cleanup if spilled.

question: If a patient's body has very low hormone levels for months, how will their target cells likely respond?

options.A: Receptor downregulation to conserve cellular energy
options.B: No change in receptor numbers on the cell membrane
options.C: Receptor upregulation to increase cellular sensitivity
options.D: Complete destruction of the hormone production glands

explanation: When hormones are scarce, cells put out more receptors—like putting out extra fishing nets—to catch every little bit of hormone that floats by. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h2)

question: Which of the following activities must a client avoid during the GTT waiting period?

options.A: Drinking small sips of plain water
options.B: Smoking cigarettes or drinking coffee
options.C: Sitting quietly in a comfortable chair
options.D: Reading a book or magazine

explanation: Nicotine and caffeine stimulate the nervous system and can alter blood glucose readings, so they are strictly prohibited. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h6)

question: Which scissors are best suited for cutting delicate, fine tissues?

options.A: Wire cutting shears
options.B: Metzenbaum scissors
options.C: Orthopedic bone cutters
options.D: Mayo heavy scissors

explanation: Metzenbaum scissors have fine, slender tips specifically designed for careful dissection of delicate internal tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of a pelvic infection after a procedure?

options.A: Foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge
options.B: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.C: Persistent fever and chills
options.D: Sudden development of normal morning appetite

explanation: Spot on! Wanting to eat normally is a sign of a happy, healing body. Fever, bad-smelling discharge, and terrible pain are the real warning signs to watch out for.

question: Why do the ureters enter the bladder wall at a slant (oblique angle)?

options.A: To allow the renal pelvis to drain more fluid at one time

options.C: To shorten the overall length of the lower ureter tract
options.D: To slow down fluid speed before it enters the bladder cavity

explanation: You're doing great! That slanted angle acts like a one-way valve, keeping urine from washing back up to the kidneys when the bladder fills up.

question: What should the nurse do immediately if a patient complains of severe burning under a poultice?

options.A: Wait another hour to see if it stops
options.B: Tie the bandage tighter to stop the burning
options.C: Tell the patient to endure the pain
options.D: Remove the poultice and wash the skin

explanation: Severe burning means the application is too hot or irritating, requiring immediate removal to prevent skin injury. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why does a patch of skin get red and swollen when it becomes inflamed?

options.A: Oil glands overproduce and trap water under the skin
options.B: Lymph channels completely shut down to trap toxins
options.C: Skin cells multiply rapidly to form a shield
options.D: Blood vessels widen and leak fluid into the nearby tissue

explanation: When inflammation hits, blood vessels open wider (causing redness) and let fluid seep into the tissue (causing that puffy swelling).

question: Why are nurse managers usually involved in management audits?

options.A: To connect executive policies with actual bedside practices
options.B: To write new financial accounting laws for the ministry of health
options.C: To punish staff members who make clinical documentation errors
options.D: To replace the hospital chief executive officer during emergencies

explanation: Nurse managers are the amazing bridge between big hospital bosses and everyday patient care. Their input helps auditors see how administrative choices truly play out on the ward!

question: A patient arrives at the emergency ward in severe pain and struggling to breathe. What should the nurse do about medication education right now?

options.A: Postpone detailed teaching until the patient is stable and comfortable
options.B: Force the patient to read a long pamphlet immediately
options.C: Give the medication silently without any explanation ever
options.D: Ask family members to sign a waiver ignoring the teaching

explanation: Severe pain and distress make it impossible to focus or remember things. Always stabilize the patient first before trying to teach!

question: Why do we apply that slippery water-based gel to a patient's skin before doing an ultrasound?

options.A: To get rid of air pockets that block sound waves
options.B: To cool down the hot scanner probe
options.C: To numb the skin so the scan doesn't hurt
options.D: To leave a mark on the skin for later

explanation: Sound waves struggle to travel through air. The gel acts like a bridge, helping the waves glide smoothly into the body.

question: What is the most important discharge instruction for a nurse to give a patient who just had a sigmoidoscopy with tissue biopsies?

options.A: Stay completely in bed until lab results come back.
options.B: Take strong pain pills to prevent soreness.
options.C: Report heavy bleeding or severe belly pain to the clinic right away.
options.D: Avoid solid food for two full days.

explanation: Spot on! Anytime tissue is sampled, patients must know which danger signs—like heavy bleeding or severe pain—mean they need to call the clinic.

question: Your patient suddenly complains of lower back pain and chills mid-transfusion. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the symptoms unless the blood pressure drops significantly
options.B: Stop the transfusion immediately and keep the vein open with saline
options.C: Leave the room quickly to fetch the attending physician
options.D: Slow the infusion rate down and give prescribed paracetamol

explanation: Trust your instincts! Back pain and chills are classic warning signs of a hemolytic reaction—stop the infusion right away.

question: The high-pressure alarm starts beeping loudly on the ventilator. As a nurse, what is a very common cause to check first?

options.A: An accidental extubation of the endotracheal tube
options.B: A deflation of the endotracheal tube cuff
options.C: A loose connection between the tubing and the patient
options.D: Secretions or mucus plug in the endotracheal tube

explanation: Think of it like a blocked straw—if mucus or a kink blocks the tube, the machine has to push harder to get air in, triggering that high-pressure alarm!

question: What three conditions make up the dangerous 'lethal triad' in severe trauma?

options.A: Hypotension, hypoxia, and polyuria
options.B: Tachycardia, alkalosis, and dehydration
options.C: Hyperglycemia, fever, and hypertension
options.D: Hypothermia, acidosis, and coagulopathy

explanation: Low body temperature, acid buildup, and poor clotting form a vicious, deadly cycle in major trauma cases.

question: Why might someone having a severe gout attack still have a normal blood uric acid level?

options.A: Blood tests cannot detect uric acid once joint pain begins
options.B: Uric acid completely disappears from the body during an acute attack
options.C: The uric acid has permanently left the bloodstream and entered the bones
options.D: Inflammatory stress and sudden hormone shifts can temporarily lower serum urate readings

explanation: Don't let this trick you! The stress of a sudden flare can temporarily drop blood uric acid levels, so a normal lab result doesn't rule out gout.

question: Which sign is a nurse most likely to notice in a newborn with an open heart shunt like PDA?

options.A: High fever accompanied by generalized body rash
options.B: Extreme weight gain within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: An abnormal heart murmur and breathing difficulty
options.D: Complete inability to pass any meconium stool

explanation: Brilliant! Extra blood swirling through unclosed shunts creates extra sounds we hear as a murmur, and extra fluid can make the baby breathe a bit faster. You're learning real clinical skills! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)

question: Why do nurses encourage patients to get up and walk around early after pelvic laparoscopy?

options.A: It stops fluid from refilling the pelvic pouch.
options.B: It speeds up internal stitch healing.
options.C: It helps prevent blood clots from forming in the legs.
options.D: It completely removes the need for pain relief.

explanation: Movement is medicine! Walking gets the blood flowing smoothly back up from the legs, keeping nasty deep vein clots away.

question: Which waste bin color is strictly designated for used sharps and needles in a Nigerian hospital ward?

options.A: Yellow bag
options.B: Green bucket
options.C: Black bin
options.D: Sharps box

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps boxes prevent needle stick injuries among healthcare workers and waste handlers. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why do you always pack a portable newborn resuscitation kit for a home birth?

options.A: All home-born babies stop breathing automatically
options.B: Respiratory depression can occur unexpectedly requiring immediate intervention
options.C: Hospital transfer is always instantaneous if the baby struggles
options.D: It is only used as a decoration to calm the family

explanation: Sometimes a baby takes a little while to catch their breath. Having a resus kit ready means you can save a life instantly right there at home.

question: What is the term for the normal, temporary hair shedding that happens after childbirth?

options.A: Androgenetic female baldness
options.B: Alopecia areata universalis
options.C: Hirsutism of the puerperium
options.D: Postpartum telogen effluvium

explanation: Fancy name, simple meaning! 'Telogen effluvium' just describes that normal phase where hair sheds after delivery before the cycle resets.

question: Which personal household item should a patient with Hepatitis B be advised NOT to share with family members?

options.A: Razors and toothbrushes
options.B: Cotton bed sheets
options.C: Glass drinking cups
options.D: Ceramic dinner plates

explanation: Spot on! Razors and toothbrushes can easily trap tiny, microscopic drops of blood, which could accidentally pass the virus to someone else in the house.

question: Why do accidental drug overdoses happen so often in young children?

options.A: Children lack the enzymes needed to digest capsules
options.B: Children often mistake colorful pills for candy
options.C: Children have faster metabolisms than adults do
options.D: Children excrete medications much slower through kidneys

explanation: Curious toddlers love to explore! They frequently mistake bright, attractive pills lying around for sweets, which is why safe storage at home is so crucial.

question: Why is connecting families to local respite care services important?

options.A: It replaces the need for professional nursing visits entirely.
options.B: It prevents caregiver burnout and supports long-term caregiving.
options.C: It permanently removes the child from the parents' custody.
options.D: It ensures that parents never have to administer medications again.

explanation: You got it! Caring for a sick child is exhausting work, and respite care gives parents a well-deserved break to rest and recharge. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h8)

question: How do specialized support cohorts differ from standard general groups?

options.A: They focus on the unique life challenges of specific populations like adolescents or pregnant women.
options.B: They require mandatory financial contributions from every attending member.
options.C: They meet exclusively inside high-security hospital surgical wards.
options.D: They exclude anyone who has been on antiretroviral medication for more than one year.

explanation: Specialized cohorts target specific groups so members can discuss challenges unique to their life stage or medical condition. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h2)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to start talking with a patient who has just suffered a heavy loss?

options.A: Provide a printed checklist of grief stages for the patient to fill out
options.B: Wait in silence until the patient explicitly asks for medical advice
options.C: Tell the patient about your own personal losses to build quick rapport
options.D: Ask open-ended questions and listen actively to the patient's story

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions open the door for patients to share their unique story without feeling pressured or rushed.

question: How does community stigma often affect families living with an HIV-positive member?

options.A: It forces local health clinics to provide free housing
options.B: It causes families to isolate themselves from others
options.C: It encourages families to seek out more social groups
options.D: It improves the family's financial stability over time

explanation: Exactly. Fear of unfair judgment and discrimination can make households withdraw from friends and community activities out of worry.

question: What does providing integrated services mean in an adolescent clinic?

options.A: Requiring both parents to attend every medical consultation with the teen
options.B: Using traditional medicine alongside modern pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: Offering multiple health services like reproductive and mental care under one roof
options.D: Combining adult and adolescent patients in the same waiting room

explanation: Integrated services mean a young person can access different types of healthcare in a single convenient location. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: How can you easily tell the difference between a vesicle and a bulla?

options.A: A vesicle contains pus while a bulla contains clear serum only
options.B: A vesicle appears on mucous membranes while a bulla appears on nails
options.C: A vesicle is smaller than 1 cm while a bulla is larger than 1 cm
options.D: A vesicle is solid and raised while a bulla is completely flat

explanation: Both are fluid-filled blisters! The only real difference is their size—bullae are just the bigger ones over 1 cm.

question: A patient feels a quick cramp during an endometrial biopsy in the clinic. What do you tell her?

options.A: Administer a full dose of general intravenous anesthesia immediately
options.B: Tell the patient that the procedure was performed incorrectly by the doctor
options.C: Call the emergency surgical team immediately for suspected uterine rupture
options.D: Explain that temporary uterine cramping is a normal response to tissue sampling

explanation: Well done! Passing tools through the cervix and taking a little tissue sample naturally causes brief, passing cramps. Reassuring your patient makes a huge difference.

question: What makes the copper IUD special compared to emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: It is only effective if taken within the first two hours
options.B: It must be swallowed as a tablet with a full glass of water
options.C: It provides ongoing long-term birth control after emergency use
options.D: It permanently stops a woman from ever having children

explanation: The copper IUD is a double-whammy: it works as emergency contraception right now, and it can stay in place to prevent pregnancy for years. Super convenient!

question: Why do clients with inherited degenerative disorders need a team of different specialists (multidisciplinary team)?

options.A: Hospital regulations require at least five different specialists for every chronic illness.
options.B: It lowers the cost of hospital care by eliminating the need for registered nurses.
options.C: The disease progressively affects multiple body systems, requiring diverse specialized expertise.
options.D: Specialists can completely cure the genetic mutation if they work together.

explanation: As different body systems break down over time, various health professionals are needed to team up for physical, nutritional, and emotional support.

question: What generally happens to the tracheostomy hole (stoma) after the tube is permanently removed?

options.A: It requires major plastic surgery to sew shut
options.B: It naturally heals closed with a simple dressing
options.C: It must be plugged with a permanent metal cap
options.D: It remains permanently open for air passage

explanation: Nature is amazing! Covered with a simple dressing, the stoma usually shrinks and closes up on its own within a few days.

question: Which of these needle gauges is the thinnest?

options.A: 25 gauge
options.B: 30 gauge
options.C: 18 gauge
options.D: 20 gauge

explanation: You rock! Remember the golden rule of needles: the higher the gauge number, the thinner the actual needle diameter.

question: Why might a patient agree with family planning advice at the clinic, but fail to practice it at home?

options.A: The medication expires too quickly
options.B: Bad weather during the journey
options.C: Fear of community or family pressure
options.D: Lack of clean clinic floors

explanation: Spot on! Patients often feel caught between great clinical advice and the heavy cultural expectations waiting back home.

question: A patient in contact isolation feels depressed and refuses to open their door for nursing care. What is your best action as a nurse?

options.A: Remove the isolation sign so family members can crowd into the room
options.B: Threaten to discharge the patient immediately if they do not cooperate with rules
options.C: Acknowledge their feelings, explain the care plan patiently, and spend extra social time with them
options.D: Leave the food tray outside and refuse to enter the room for the rest of the shift

explanation: You've got a true nursing heart! Validating their feelings and showing extra care helps ease their anxiety while keeping safety standards strong.

question: Why does the pressure to have a baby boy often weigh so heavily on mothers in patriarchal societies?

options.A: Because society ties a woman's worth and security to producing a son
options.B: Because female children require more expensive healthcare services
options.C: Because local laws fine families that do not have a male child
options.D: Because boys are biologically easier to raise during infancy

explanation: In many traditional setups, a woman's peace of mind and place in the home are unfairly linked to bearing a male heir.

question: What is the main goal of giving someone a vaccine?

options.A: To provide temporary ready-made antibodies that last for one week
options.B: To physically block viruses from entering the body through the skin
options.C: To destroy all normal bacteria living inside the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: To stimulate memory cell production without causing severe disease

explanation: Vaccines introduce safe pieces of a germ so your immune system can build memory cells without you getting sick.

question: In which zone of the surgical suite are hospital staff still allowed to wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Unrestricted zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Sterile core zone
options.D: Semi-restricted zone

explanation: The unrestricted zone is the front area where you enter and receive patients before changing into your fresh theatre scrubs. Easy peasy!

question: Why do fungal infections of the toenails (onychomycosis) usually need oral pills instead of just a surface cream?

options.A: Topical creams cannot penetrate deeply enough through the hard nail plate
options.B: Fungi living in toenails are completely immune to all topical antifungal creams
options.C: Topical medications wash away too quickly from the foot due to sweat
options.D: Nail infections are always caused by systemic internal organ failure

explanation: Correct! The nail plate is thick and tough, acting like a shield that surface creams can't pass through. Pills are needed to reach the fungus from within.

question: How do seasonal disease trends influence how a nurse orders ward supplies?

options.A: They help nurses anticipate higher demand and order specific items ahead of time
options.B: They remove the need to calculate lead times when submitting requisitions
options.C: They dictate the exact time of day nurses must count the inventory
options.D: They change the physical maximum storage capacity of the drug cupboard

explanation: Anticipating disease patterns allows the ward to stock up on relevant treatments before an outbreak or seasonal surge hits. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which of these tasks is usually handled by a nursing assistant rather than a Registered Nurse (RN)?

options.A: Assisting with daily bathing and dressing
options.B: Creating the master patient care plan
options.C: Administering intravenous medications
options.D: Diagnosing new chronic health conditions

explanation: Nursing assistants are fantastic at providing direct, hands-on personal care to keep patients comfortable and clean every day.

question: How do you know a mother is truly in labor rather than experiencing false labor?

options.A: presence of lower back pain
options.B: progressive cervical dilation
options.C: mild irregular uterine tightening
options.D: rupture of the amniotic membranes

explanation: Great job thinking through this! True labor always brings real changes to the cervix—specifically opening it up (dilation)—while false labor does not.

question: Which sign points strongly to severe dehydration in a cholera patient?

options.A: Swollen ankles and high blood pressure
options.B: High fever and flushed red skin
options.C: Rapid weight gain from fluid retention
options.D: Sunken eyes and poor skin turgor

explanation: When the body lacks water, the eyes look sunken and the skin loses its snap, taking longer to bounce back when pinched.

question: What molecule builds up inside muscle cells to help them relax when a beta-2 agonist is used?

options.A: Cyclic AMP (cAMP)
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Calcium ions
options.D: Phosphodiesterase

explanation: When beta-2 agonists do their magic, they boost cAMP levels inside the cell, which tells the muscle to relax and let go of the tightness.

question: A patient taking a new blood pressure medication suddenly feels very dizzy and lightheaded when standing up. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to run in place to improve blood circulation
options.B: Administer a stimulant medication to raise the blood pressure
options.C: Check the patient's blood pressure and pulse immediately
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled clinic visit to report the finding

explanation: Dizziness after starting a new blood pressure drug points to orthostatic hypotension, requiring a check of vital signs. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: If local stores see a drop in meat sales and a huge spike in cheap instant noodles, what does this usually tell us?

options.A: Improved local agricultural output of grain-based factory foods
options.B: An unexpected surplus of manufacturing capacity for wheat products
options.C: A sudden cultural shift favoring processed instant meals over cooking
options.D: Decreased household purchasing power altering dietary choices

explanation: When people have less money, they buy cheaper comfort foods, changing their overall diet quality.

question: What is the quick check a nurse does every time they put on an N95 to check the seal called?

options.A: Qualitative sweet test
options.B: Sterile pressure scan
options.C: Manufacturer inspection
options.D: User seal check

explanation: It is a quick self-check you do every single time you put on your respirator to make sure it is sitting right.

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a joint arthroscopy?

options.A: Direct visualization and repair of internal joint structures
options.B: Removal of excess fluid trapped in the joint bursa
options.C: Measurement of bone mineral density in the hip and spine
options.D: Testing the speed of nerve impulses across the joint

explanation: Arthroscopy uses a tiny camera inserted right into the joint. It lets the surgeon look around and fix problems like torn cartilage all in one go!

question: What happens right after a single sperm successfully enters an egg?

options.A: The placenta starts producing progesterone
options.B: The embryo immediately implants into the ovary
options.C: The mother's hormone levels drop sharply
options.D: The egg blocks other sperm from entering

explanation: Smart egg! To keep everything balanced, the egg instantly changes its outer layer so no other sperm can squeeze in.

question: What shape is the anterior (front) fontanelle?

options.A: Round-shaped
options.B: Diamond-shaped
options.C: Oval-shaped
options.D: Triangle-shaped

explanation: You got it! The anterior fontanelle sits right at the front and is famously diamond-shaped.

question: What happens inside the body to cause lymphoma?

options.A: Lymph vessels become blocked and burst
options.B: Abnormal lymphocytes multiply out of control and form tumors
options.C: The spleen stops filtering old cells
options.D: Bone marrow permanently stops making white cells

explanation: Lymphoma happens when those protective white blood cells (lymphocytes) go wild, dividing without stopping and building up in the lymph nodes.

question: What is the most important fluid instruction to give a patient taking an expectorant?

options.A: Take the dose with a single dry swallow without any liquid
options.B: Encourage high water intake to help thin the mucus secretions
options.C: Restrict all fluids for two hours before and after taking the pill
options.D: Mix the medication only in thick milk or orange juice

explanation: Exactly! The drug needs water in the body to actually do its job of liquefying that stubborn mucus.

question: Why must you feel (palpate) both rods of a Jadelle implant before trying to remove them?

options.A: To check if the hormone has completely changed color inside the body
options.B: To confirm the exact location of each rod and avoid missing a retained piece
options.C: To measure how much weight the client has gained since the insertion date
options.D: To make sure the local anesthetic has completely frozen the entire arm

explanation: Since Jadelle has two rods, you always want to locate both beforehand so you don't accidentally leave one behind in the arm!

question: Which mistake during a cervical swab can ruin the lab result?

options.A: Explaining the testing procedure to the patient too early
options.B: Using a plastic speculum instead of a cold metal one
options.C: Allowing the patient to empty their bladder before the exam
options.D: Leaving excess mucus on the cervix before taking the sample

explanation: You got it! Too much mucus or discharge blocks the cells, making it impossible for the lab tech to read the sample accurately.
